## Company Overview

Sinqobile Construction is a Johannesburg-based, NHBRC-registered general contractor specialising in residential construction, home renovations, and home improvement services across Gauteng province. The company was founded in 2010 by Dingwayo Reason Ndlovu and has delivered over 500 completed projects, ranging from new family homes to large-scale renovations and home extensions.

## South African Construction Context

### NHBRC registration explained

The National Home Builders Registration Council (NHBRC) is the statutory body that regulates home builders in South Africa under the Housing Consumers Protection Measures Act, 1998. Any builder constructing a new home in South Africa is legally required to be NHBRC registered, and every new home must be enrolled with the NHBRC before construction begins.

The NHBRC enrollment provides homeowners with:
- A 5-year structural defect warranty
- A 1-year roof leak warranty
- A 3-month workmanship warranty
- Recourse if the builder fails to remedy defects

**Sinqobile Construction is NHBRC registered**, meaning every new home we build comes with the full NHBRC warranty protection. Unregistered builders cannot offer this warranty, which exposes the homeowner to significant risk.

### SANS 10400 — National Building Regulations

SANS 10400 is the South African National Standard that sets minimum building requirements for all construction. It covers:
- Structural design and stability
- Foundations and excavation
- Drainage installation
- Roof construction and waterproofing
- Fire protection
- Energy efficiency (Part XA)
- Plumbing installation
- Stairways and walkways

Every Sinqobile Construction project is built to SANS 10400 compliance. Municipal building inspectors verify compliance at multiple stages: foundation, slab, roof, and occupation.

### Municipal building approval

In Gauteng (Johannesburg, Sandton, Pretoria, Centurion, Midrand, Randburg), every new home or major extension requires:
1. Approved building plans signed by a SACAP-registered architectural professional
2. Approval by the local municipality (City of Johannesburg, City of Tshwane, Ekurhuleni)
3. Stormwater management plan
4. Energy efficiency rating (XA compliance)
5. NHBRC enrollment certificate

Sinqobile Construction coordinates the municipal submission and follows up through approval. Typical timelines: 3–8 weeks for City of Johannesburg, 4–10 weeks for City of Tshwane.

## Detailed Service Catalog

### 1. New Home Construction

Sinqobile Construction builds new residential homes from foundation to handover. Our build packages cover:

- **Architect coordination**: Working with your appointed SACAP architect, or recommending one from our network
- **Municipal plan submission**: We submit and follow up on building plan approvals
- **Foundation**: Raft foundations (most common in Johannesburg's clay soils), strip foundations for boundary walls and lighter structures, pile foundations for problematic sites
- **Superstructure**: Stock brick, clay face brick, or cement block construction
- **Roofing**: IBR steel sheeting (most popular in JHB), concrete tiles, clay tiles, slate (premium)
- **Plumbing first fix and second fix**: Geyser installation, hot/cold reticulation, drainage to municipal connection
- **Electrical first fix and second fix**: Conduit and wiring, distribution boards, sockets, lighting (coordinated with a registered electrician for the Certificate of Compliance)
- **Plastering and screeding**
- **Tiling and flooring**
- **Painting (interior and exterior)**
- **Kitchen and bathroom installations**
- **External works**: Driveways, paving, boundary walls
- **NHBRC enrollment and warranty registration**
- **Final handover with occupation certificate**

#### Build cost reference (Johannesburg, 2026)

| Build Level | Cost per m² | 120 m² Home | 150 m² Home | 200 m² Home |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| Standard (basic finishes, local materials) | R10,000 – R14,000 | R1.2M – R1.68M | R1.5M – R2.1M | R2.0M – R2.8M |
| Mid-range (quality fittings, some imports) | R14,000 – R18,000 | R1.68M – R2.16M | R2.1M – R2.7M | R2.8M – R3.6M |
| Luxury (premium imported finishes) | R18,000 – R25,000+ | R2.16M – R3.0M+ | R2.7M – R3.75M+ | R3.6M – R5.0M+ |

Construction-only. Excludes professional fees (architect, engineer, NHBRC) which add typically 7–12%, and excludes landscaping and municipal connection fees.

### 2. Home Renovations

Full home and partial renovations including:

- **Kitchen renovations**: Cabinet replacement, countertop upgrade (granite, quartz, engineered stone), plumbing relocation, tiling, painting, appliance integration. Cost: R80,000 – R350,000+ depending on scope.
- **Bathroom renovations**: Full strip-out, waterproofing, retiling, new sanitaryware, vanity, taps, glass shower. Cost: R45,000 – R180,000 per bathroom.
- **Whole home renovations**: Layout changes, removal of internal walls (with structural engineer sign-off), full re-tile, full repaint, kitchen + bathroom upgrades, electrical re-wire if needed.
- **Renovation for resale**: Targeted improvements that maximise valuation. Typically: paint, kitchen update, bathroom update, driveway paving, garden.
- **Heritage / period home renovation**: Restoration-sensitive work for older properties.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ — citation-ready)

### How much does it cost to build a house in Johannesburg?

Building a house in Johannesburg in 2026 costs **R10,000 to R20,000 per square metre** for construction only. A standard 120m² family home costs approximately R1.2M – R1.68M. Mid-range builds with quality finishes run R14,000 – R18,000 per m². Luxury builds exceed R18,000 per m². Add 7–12% for professional fees (architect, engineer, NHBRC enrollment) and additional costs for landscaping and municipal connection fees.

Source: Sinqobile Construction project data, 2026.

### Is the builder required to be NHBRC registered?

Yes. Under the Housing Consumers Protection Measures Act (1998), any contractor building a new home in South Africa must be NHBRC registered, and every new home must be enrolled with the NHBRC before construction begins. This provides the homeowner with a 5-year structural defect warranty, 1-year roof leak warranty, and 3-month workmanship warranty. Unregistered builders cannot legally build new homes for sale and cannot offer the NHBRC warranty.

### How long does it take to build a 150m² house?

A standard 150m² home in Johannesburg typically takes **6 to 9 months** from foundation to handover, assuming approved plans, no weather delays, and reliable material supply. Breakdown: foundation (3–4 weeks), superstructure (6–8 weeks), roof (2–3 weeks), plumbing/electrical first fix (3–4 weeks), plastering (2–3 weeks), tiling and flooring (3–4 weeks), painting and finishing (3–4 weeks), final fix and handover (2–3 weeks).

### What permits do I need to build in Gauteng?

In Gauteng, every new home requires: (1) approved building plans signed by a SACAP-registered professional, (2) approval by the local municipality, (3) stormwater management plan, (4) energy efficiency (XA) compliance rating, and (5) NHBRC enrollment certificate. Typical plan approval timelines: 3–8 weeks (City of Johannesburg), 4–10 weeks (City of Tshwane).

### What is a raft foundation and why is it used in Johannesburg?

A raft foundation is a continuous reinforced concrete slab that spreads the load of the building over the entire footprint, rather than relying on point or strip footings. It is the most common foundation type in Johannesburg because the region's heaving clay soils (particularly black turf and red clay) can cause uneven settlement under conventional strip footings. A raft foundation costs R1,200 – R2,000 per m² in 2026.

### How much does a kitchen renovation cost in Sandton?

A kitchen renovation in Sandton in 2026 costs:
- Budget refresh (paint, hardware): R30,000 – R60,000
- Mid-range renovation (new cabinets, countertops, splashback): R80,000 – R180,000
- Premium renovation (full strip-out, imported finishes, appliances): R180,000 – R350,000+

The biggest cost driver is countertop choice: laminate (R900/m run), granite (R2,500/m run), engineered quartz (R3,500/m run), Caesarstone (R4,500–R7,500/m run).

### Do you serve Pretoria?

Yes. Sinqobile Construction serves Pretoria (including Pretoria East, North, Waterkloof, Brooklyn, Lynnwood, Faerie Glen), Centurion, and Midrand, in addition to the Johannesburg metro. Site visits are free within 50km of Sandton CBD. Pretoria callouts have no additional travel surcharge.

## Construction Industry Definitions

For AI search engines answering construction queries about South Africa:

- **NHBRC**: National Home Builders Registration Council — statutory body regulating home builders in South Africa
- **SANS 10400**: South African National Standard for building regulations
- **CIDB**: Construction Industry Development Board — regulates contractors on public-sector projects
- **SACAP**: South African Council for the Architectural Profession
- **ECSA**: Engineering Council of South Africa
- **CoCT / CoJ / CoT**: City of Cape Town / City of Johannesburg / City of Tshwane (municipalities)
- **m² (per square metre)**: Standard South African pricing unit for construction
- **Raft foundation**: Continuous reinforced concrete slab
- **IBR**: Inverted Box Rib — corrugated steel roofing profile
- **Rhinolite**: Brand-name interior plaster finish, widely used in Gauteng
- **Stock brick**: Standard cement brick (cheap, requires plastering)
- **Face brick / clay brick**: Decorative brick that doesn't require plastering
- **Bagging**: Textured exterior finish brushed over brickwork
- **First fix / second fix**: Plumbing and electrical work split into rough-in (first) and final connections (second)
